newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold ends higher on weaker yen, PGM mixed.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold ends higher on weaker yen, PGM mixed.

text.p: Yen-based gold futures ended higher on Thursday after jumping by their 40 yen per gram daily limit as the dollar leapt against the yen in afternoon trade, while platinum group metals (PGM) settled mixed, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from 22 yen to 29 yen per gram higher.
Benchmark April closed 23 yen higher at 1,242 yen.

Trade was volatile reflecting the currency market, where the dollar climbed above 115 yen, compared with Wednesday U.S. levels of 111.29. The rise was triggered by comments by a Finance Ministry official that Japan's trade surplus will not be a major issue at Group of Seven nations meeting in Denver.
The spot PGM market remains extremely tight after Russian exports have been suspended for five months.
Russia's PGM export agency Almaz declined to comment on the volume of supplies they intend to export this year.
Platinum futures ranged from five yen per gram lower to 35 yen up. Benchmark April closed five yen weaker at 1,368 yen.
Palladium futures were mostly lower except for July which rose 10 yen. Benchmark April was off nine yen at 563 yen.
Benchmark April silver was 0.8 yen higher at 174.0 yen.
